correctness.rationale: For p>=11, p=11 mod12, Legendre(-1)=-1 and Legendre(3)=1, and in cyclic multiplicative group order 2q the primitive roots are exactly the nonresidues other than -1. If p=7 mod8, a=(p-1)/2, b=(p-3)/2 have a+b=p-2 and abc≡b. If p=3 mod8, a=2 primitive; the exact character sum Σχ(x(x+2))=-1 and linear sums give (p-3)/4 residues with χ(b)=χ(b+2)=-1, of which b=p-3 uniquely violates the representatives/primitive conditions. Hence (p-7)/4 witnesses; the product cannot be -1 because (b+1)^2=1/2 is impossible when χ(2)=-1. p=5,7 checked by listing primitive roots. Independent order tests validated all safe primes p<1000, while the proof is for all safe primes.
residual_risks: Infinitude of safe primes is not known; theorem is conditional on the existence of such p.
Exact count is only for a=2 in p≡3 mod8 class, not a census of all ordered witnesses.
